forecastingPrinciples.why: A business without a forecast is flying blind. Forecasting allows TCD to make confident hiring, inventory, marketing, and investment decisions.
forecastingPrinciples.frequency: Update rolling 12-month revenue forecast monthly. Update 13-week cashflow forecast weekly.
forecastingPrinciples.accuracy: A forecast doesn't need to be perfect — it needs to be directionally correct and updated regularly. ±15% is acceptable; ±30%+ signals a process problem.

pipelineMethod.description: Weight pipeline opportunities by probability of close and expected timeline
pipelineMethod.formula: Forecast Revenue = Sum of (Deal Value × Close Probability) for all open opportunities

historicalMethod.description: Use trailing 12-month average monthly revenue + known seasonality adjustments

seasonalFactors.Q1_JanMar: 0.85 — typically slower start, January particularly quiet

expenseForecasting.forecastingRule: Fixed costs are knowable to ±5%. Variable costs should be modelled as % of revenue. Contingency: add 8% to all expense forecasts for unplanned costs.

scenarioPlanning.base: Most likely outcome — pipeline weighted by stage probability
scenarioPlanning.upside: Base × 1.25 — if 2–3 large pipeline deals close faster than expected
scenarioPlanning.downside: Base × 0.70 — if 2–3 deals stall or are pushed to next quarter
scenarioPlanning.action: Model all 3 scenarios. In downside: what costs can be reduced? In upside: what resource constraints emerge?
scenarioPlanning.breakEven: Know your monthly break-even revenue — the revenue needed to cover all operating costs. This is the single most important number for a small business CEO.
